question_text: Let A = {x ∈ Z : x^2 ≤ 9} and B = {x ∈ N : x < 5}, where N is the set of positive integers. What is n(A ∩ B)?
For two finite sets A and B, n(A) = 18, n(B) = 25 and n(A ∪ B) = 35. Find n(A \ B).
explanation: Using n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B), we get 35 = 18 + 25 - n(A ∩ B), so n(A ∩ B) = 8. Therefore n(A \ B) = n(A) - n(A ∩ B) = 18 - 8 = 10.

question_text: Let U = {1, 2, 3, ..., 20}. Let A be the set of multiples of 2 in U and B be the set of multiples of 3 in U. Find n((A ∪ B)').
explanation: In U, multiples of 2 are 10 in number and multiples of 3 are 6 in number. Multiples of both 2 and 3, i.e. multiples of 6, are 3 in number. Thus n(A ∪ B) = 10 + 6 - 3 = 13. Hence n((A ∪ B)') = 20 - 13 = 7.

question_text: For two finite sets A and B, n(A ∪ B) = 42, n(A △ B) = 30 and n(A) = 25, where A △ B denotes the symmetric difference of A and B. Find n(B).
explanation: The symmetric difference contains elements belonging to exactly one of A and B. Since n(A ∪ B) = 42 and n(A △ B) = 30, we have n(A ∩ B) = 42 - 30 = 12. Therefore n(A \ B) = 25 - 12 = 13. Since n(A △ B) = n(A \ B) + n(B \ A), we get n(B \ A) = 30 - 13 = 17. Hence n(B) = n(B \ A) + n(A ∩ B) = 17 + 12 = 29.

question_text: Let A, B and C be subsets of a universal set having 30 elements. Suppose n(A) = n(B) = n(C) = 15 and no element belongs to all three sets. What is the minimum possible value of n(A ∪ B ∪ C)?
explanation: The total number of memberships across A, B and C is 15 + 15 + 15 = 45. Since no element belongs to all three sets, each element of A ∪ B ∪ C can contribute at most 2 memberships. Therefore n(A ∪ B ∪ C) must be at least ceiling(45/2) = 23. This value is achievable, for example by taking 22 elements belonging to exactly two of the sets and 1 element belonging to exactly one set, arranged to make each set have 15 elements. Hence the minimum possible value is 23.
